title: Discrete Centered Hypercontractivity
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with mean zero, and suppose there is a finite set supporting $X$ almost everywhere such that every point in that set has probability at least $\lambda$. If $q>2$ and $0<\lambda\le1$, set $\rho=\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/(2\sqrt{q-1})$. Then $X$ is affine hypercontractive both from exponent $2$ to exponent $q$ with parameter $\rho$, and from exponent $q/(q-1)$ to exponent $2$ with parameter $\rho$: in each case the exponents satisfy the required order, $0\le\rho<1$, $X$ belongs to the target $L^q$ space, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_{\text{target}}\le\|a+bX\|_{\text{source}}$ for all real $a,b$.
hypotheses_covered: X is a real-valued function on Ω
X has a finite almost-everywhere support whose point masses are at least λ
The integral of X with respect to μ is zero
replaced: Let $q>2$, $0<\lambda\le1$, and let $X$ be measurable and centered on a probability space, supported almost surely on a finite set whose atoms each have mass at least $\lambda$. Setting $\rho=\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/(2\sqrt{q-1})$, both $H_{2,q,\rho}(X)$ and $H_{q/(q-1),2,\rho}(X)$ hold. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
